utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel, everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Mathias Neuner, Daryl Mundis, the case manager Andres Vatter, and I anticipate that Ms, Tecla Henry-Benjamin will be joining us shortly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before giving the floor to Defence counsel for their appearances, shall we go into open session because I see we're in closed session. And on the transcript it says Wednesday, though are Thursday. Today is Thursday.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the transcript will be corrected, and will indicate Thursday instead of Wednesday and it should be the 17th of June. Can we have the appearances for the Defence, now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, good morning Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, defence counsel, Stephane Bourgon, and Muriel Cauvin, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber and the Judges bid good morning to all those present, to the representatives of the Prosecution, of the Defence, the accused, all the staff of this courtroom, and Madam court reporter. We will in a moment continue with the testimony of the witness. I call on the Defence to make sure that as far as the first accused is concerned, that they complete their examination today. This should be done so as to allow the other Defence team to have an hour and a half as they requested because it is quite possible that the Prosecution and the Judges may have additional questions. Does Mr. Mundis have an observation to make at this stage of the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution does indeed have an observation to make. Earlier, the Prosecution indicated that we were not in possession of the written diaries of the witness. It turns out, Mr. President, that due to the alertness of a member of additional -- of a different trial team who is temporarily assigned to our case, in reading the transcript this attorney alerted me to the fact that we do in fact have the diaries. We have the diaries covering the period from August 1991 through the end of 1994. We immediately took steps yesterday to disclose those handwritten diaries to the Defence, which was completed early in the evening yesterday. We have translations of only the period covering about August 20th, 1993, through the 3rd or 4th of October, 1993, focussing on a different case. I have asked the investigation commander to undertake an investigation as to why this was not -- why this material didn't turn up in the electronic searches which the Prosecution has undertaken. The preliminary explanation which I received was the fact that the diaries are obviously handwritten; the search engines that we use to locate material is based on an OCR or optical character reader. The OCR technology has a very difficult time with handwritten material, and an examination of the diary indicates that the witness or his own name only appears in several locations within the diary which is as one would expect, the witness would not be referring to himself by his own name. As a result of that, our preliminary indications are that the technology was unable to recognise his handwritten name in the material, which is why it did not come up on an electronic search. Further inquiries are being made in this matter. Again, the Prosecution assures the Trial Chamber and the Defence that we are doing everything possible to comply with our disclosure obligations. This material, as I said, was disclosed to the Defence last evening, and assuming that the Trial Chamber would like that material we can take steps to either provide the original or photocopy of the original and the translated portions that we do have, or we can certainly submit whichever portions of that diary the Trial Chamber would like to have translated into English or French or both. Obviously, the total is 560 handwritten pages. That will take a significant period of time to get translated. But if the Chamber wants that or certain portions of that, we will request translations to be made. And as I said, we will provide the Trial Chamber with whatever part or all of that material that the Trial Chamber thinks would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that one of your colleagues realised that this diary was already in the possession of the Prosecution, and you are telling us that through electronic search engines you were unable to detect it earlier. But as this diary has been found, you can provide the Chamber not the 560 pages, of course, but only the entries that correspond to the testimony of the witness. On this point, has the Defence anything to tell us?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is quite true that my learned friend informed us late yesterday afternoon that they have found this diary, and about 7.00 p.m. the diary was provided to the Defence. Of course, we haven't had the time to review such voluminous material by this morning, but it is the position of the Defence of General Hadzihasanovic that we will continue with our cross-examination and only should the study of this diary lead to any additional questions that should be put to the witness, we will in that case request that the witness be recalled for additional examination. Thank you. Let us hear the other Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have nothing further to add to what Ms. Residovic has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will in a moment during the break discuss the matter amongst ourselves and let you know what our position is. As far as I'm concerned, I'm able to say that I'm looking forward with impatience to the investigator who is going to testify next week. I have a number of technical questions to put to him; namely, what he does when he has a witness and when he shows him documents. We have seen that it is possible to show the witness a document when he recognises it, but if a witness has a document in his possession, what does the investigator do? Does he ask him to provide a copy? Does he make a report saying that he has received a copy? There are a series of technical issues that should they be dealt with in advance, then these problems would not arise. If there's a list of documents that were discussed with the witness by the investigator, then we wouldn't be having this type of problem. And of course, I will look through the Rules and see if there is any need to contact the competent authorities with regard to this. We have taken up 10 minutes of time, but without further ado, we shall now call in the witness. And go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 18th day of June, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
